title: Derived slice composites are left derived functors of the ordinary composites
statement: For X, U and f as in the completed adic slice scalar comparison, write A for the R-modules on X. The composite of exact derived slice restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] with the derived slice scalar extension [def-weil-pbc-completed-adic-slice-scalar-extension], and the composite of the derived scalar extension along f [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] with exact derived slice restriction, each admit a natural transformation from their composite with the localization K(A) -> D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the localized ordinary composite (slice restriction followed by slice scalar extension, respectively scalar extension followed by slice restriction, applied termwise to complexes), exhibiting it as a left derived functor of that ordinary composite along the quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 0G7E and 0D6D: K-flat resolution, pullback preservation, and universal counits

proof.text: Let P be the class of homotopy-category objects represented by K-flat complexes. Every homotopy object admits a quasi-isomorphism from P by the independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem.

Compose the exact restriction factorization isomorphisms with the universal counits of the chosen derived scalar extensions, and then the termwise-composition isomorphism on homotopy categories. This constructs the two required counits to the ordinary composites.

Both composite counits are invertible on P: for restriction followed by scalar extension, exact slice restriction preserves K-flat complexes, and the slice scalar-extension counit is invertible there; for scalar extension followed by restriction, apply exact derived restriction to the invertible global scalar-extension counit. The homotopy-quotient factorization isomorphism identifies the restricted representative in the first case.

A candidate counit invertible on P makes its ordinary functor invert quasi-isomorphisms between members of P, by naturality. Apply the existing resolving-class theorem to obtain a universal pair, also invertible on P. The universal lift from the candidate to that pair is invertible on P by the counit factorization equation. Every homotopy object has a quasi-isomorphic resolution in P, so naturality makes this lift invertible on all localization images. Fully faithful precomposition by the localization reflects this isomorphism. The universal-lift criterion therefore proves that the candidate itself is a left derived functor. Apply this to each composite counit.
